attributes.description: Rare-event and behaviour-focused views. Use alongside the Overview dashboard: Overview shows what fired most, this shows what looks wrong.
attributes.title: Hayabusa - Threat Hunting

attributes.description: Hayabusa detections (hayabusa-mission-*) and every raw event (hayabusa-raw-*) of the mission on one timeline, through the data view 'Mission - everything'. Filter a host: its detections, its activity and the events around each detection, together.
attributes.title: Mission timeline - detections and raw events

attributes.description: The ATT&CK view of the Hayabusa detections: tactics, techniques, where and when. Only detections whose Sigma rule carries an ATT&CK tag appear here (see the first panel for how many). The query bar hides this tool's own collection activity (tags: evtxer-collection); clear it to see that too.
attributes.title: Hayabusa - MITRE ATT&CK

attributes.description: Windows event log detections from Hayabusa (Sigma rules). Severity is higher = worse (critical 99 ... informational 1) -- note Suricata data elsewhere in Security Onion uses the opposite scale.
attributes.title: Hayabusa - EVTX Detection Overview

attributes.description: PEAK-style baseline hunting on Hayabusa detections: every table is sorted so the RARE answers come first, because noise repeats and intrusions mostly do not. Start at panel 1, click a value to filter the whole dashboard, then open Discover for the raw detections. Only events that matched a rule are here, not every log record. The query bar hides this tool's own collection activity (tags: evtxer-collection); clear it to see that too.
attributes.title: Hayabusa - PEAK Hunt

attributes.description: The domain controllers' story from EVERY raw event (hayabusa-raw-*): DCSync, directory changes, delegation and SPNs, account flags, SID history, trusts, password resets, certificate requests and Kerberos encryption over time. Most panels need the DCs' Security logs; the four Kerberos hunts (kerberoasting, AS-REP, spraying, PKINIT) are on 'Raw Events - PEAK Hunt'.
attributes.title: Raw Events - Active Directory

attributes.description: Seven anomaly hunts beyond 'rarest first': only on one machine, new lately, odd hours (UTC), wrong place, bursts, fan-out, longest command lines. On real machines start with sections 4, 6 and 7, then use 1 and 2 as leads. Every Windows event EVTXER sent, so its own collection visit (wevtutil, its staging folder) shows here too.
attributes.title: Raw Events - Anomaly Hunt

attributes.description: PEAK baseline hunting on EVERY Windows event EVTXER sent (hayabusa-raw-*), not only the ones Hayabusa flagged. Tables are sorted so the RARE answers come first. Time = when the event happened (@timestamp). Pivot from a Hayabusa detection: host.name + winlog.channel + winlog.record_id finds its raw event; then widen to the host.
attributes.title: Raw Events - PEAK Hunt

attributes.description: How an intruder moved between machines, from EVERY Windows event EVTXER sent (hayabusa-raw-*): hidden shares and named pipes, PsExec and its relatives, RDP sessions, which source logged on to which host, outbound connections. Remote logons by account and RDP 1149 are on 'Raw Events - PEAK Hunt'. Time = when the event happened.
attributes.title: Raw Events - Lateral Movement

attributes.description: How an intruder stays and hides, from EVERY raw event (hayabusa-raw-*): autostart registry, WMI subscriptions, BITS jobs, unsigned DLLs and drivers, files dropped in user folders, injection, PowerShell modules, Defender and firewall changes, audit policy. New services, tasks and cleared logs are on 'Raw Events - PEAK Hunt'. Many panels need Sysmon: 'No results' is an honest answer.
attributes.title: Raw Events - Persistence & Evasion

attributes.description: Hayabusa's own Results Summary (the end-of-scan screen and HTML report), rebuilt from the uploaded detections: totals and unique rules per level, the busiest day per level, the computers with the most distinct detections, every alert, the timeline, and a logon summary. Events that matched no rule are not uploaded, so Hayabusa's 'Total events analyzed' and 'Data reduction' are in the Convert tab's COVERAGE line instead. The query bar hides this tool's own collection activity (tags: evtxer-collection); clear it to see that too.
attributes.title: Hayabusa - Results Summary

attributes.title: hayabusa-raw-*

attributes.description: The machine-days with the most events, busiest first (days are UTC). Compare a machine with its own other days. Hayabusa detections only - its informational rules record many ordinary events, so this works on plain Elastic too, thinner than the raw view.
attributes.title: 5. Bursts - busiest machine-days, all events

attributes.description: Failed logons per machine per day (UTC), busiest first: password guessing and spraying. Security 4625. Hayabusa detections only - its informational rules record many ordinary events, so this works on plain Elastic too, thinner than the raw view.

query.query: (winlog.channel: "Security" and event.code: "4625")

attributes.title: 5. Bursts - busiest machine-days, failed logons

attributes.description: Every event per machine over time. A bright cell in a dull row is a burst: password spraying, mass file access, a stuck process. Hayabusa detections only - its informational rules record many ordinary events, so this works on plain Elastic too, thinner than the raw view.
attributes.title: 5. Bursts - events per machine over time

attributes.description: Logons per machine per weekday. A weekend logon on a weekday-only machine stands out. Security 4624. Hours and days are UTC - event logs store UTC; the target's own time zone is not in the data. Hayabusa detections only - its informational rules record many ordinary events, so this works on plain Elastic too, thinner than the raw view.

query.query: (winlog.channel: "Security" and event.code: "4624")

attributes.title: 3. Odd hours - logons by day of week (UTC)

attributes.description: One account logging on to many machines is lateral movement - or an admin account; know which. Security 4624; Windows' built-in accounts are left out. Hayabusa detections only - its informational rules record many ordinary events, so this works on plain Elastic too, thinner than the raw view.

query.query: ((winlog.channel: "Security" and event.code: "4624")) and user.name: * and not op.BuiltinAccount: true

attributes.title: 6. Fan-out - accounts logging on to the most machines

attributes.description: A machine logged on to from many places: a file server is normal, a workstation is not. Security 4624. Hayabusa detections only - its informational rules record many ordinary events, so this works on plain Elastic too, thinner than the raw view.

query.query: ((winlog.channel: "Security" and event.code: "4624")) and winlog.event_data.IpAddress: * and not winlog.event_data.IpAddress: ("-" or "::1" or "127.0.0.1")

attributes.title: 6. Fan-out - machines reached from the most sources

attributes.description: One source trying many accounts is password spraying. Security 4625; sources without an IP (local logons) are not ranked. Hayabusa detections only - its informational rules record many ordinary events, so this works on plain Elastic too, thinner than the raw view.

query.query: ((winlog.channel: "Security" and event.code: "4625")) and winlog.event_data.IpAddress: * and not winlog.event_data.IpAddress: ("-" or "::1" or "127.0.0.1") and not op.BuiltinAccount: true

attributes.description: Logons per machine per hour of the day. Work happens in office hours; 03:00 stands out. Security 4624. Hours and days are UTC - event logs store UTC; the target's own time zone is not in the data. Hayabusa detections only - its informational rules record many ordinary events, so this works on plain Elastic too, thinner than the raw view.

attributes.title: 3. Odd hours - logons by hour (UTC)

attributes.description: Programs and PowerShell started per machine per hour. Program starts come from Sysmon event 1, else Security 4688 (process-creation auditing). PowerShell starts: Windows PowerShell 400. A machine that records program starts in BOTH Sysmon (event 1) and Windows' own auditing (4688) counts each start twice. Hours and days are UTC - event logs store UTC; the target's own time zone is not in the data. Hayabusa detections only - its informational rules record many ordinary events, so this works on plain Elastic too, thinner than the raw view.

attributes.description: A file given a stream: mostly Zone.Identifier, the mark Windows puts on a download - its HostUrl (in the event's Contents, when Sysmon keeps them - open it in Discover) says where it came from. A stream on an .exe, or a stream with another name, is hiding data. Sysmon 15.

attributes.description: Run / RunOnce keys, Image File Execution Options (debugger hijack), Winlogon (Shell, Userinit), a service's ImagePath or ServiceDll, LSA packages (a new SSP reads passwords), AppInit_DLLs, a user's own COM server (hijacking) and Office add-ins: what starts by itself. attributes.title: 8. Drivers loaded (Sysmon 6) - rarest first
